nodes.label: ROMI Formula (Incremental Contribution Margin / Marketing Spend)
nodes.rationale: ROAS (gross revenue over spend, no incrementality or margin) is deliberately excluded from the reference set because it can't fail — a channel with terrible margins and zero incremental effect can still post a large ROAS. State the COGS assumption out loud and re-run the number at a band around it every time; the sensitivity check is what turns 'trust this number' into something a reader can audit.

nodes.label: Economics of Error Worksheet
nodes.rationale: Don't assume a decision is atomic — a single-looking action (react to campaign performance, adjust a bid) routinely bundles a cheap reversible half with an expensive hard-to-reverse one; scoring the bundle as one tier always gets one half wrong, so the worksheet forces the four questions per sub-action even when the resulting tiers land asymmetrically.

nodes.label: Governance Table (per-agent failure/control/kill-switch)
nodes.rationale: The main table is the part every team fills in under audit pressure; the exclusions table is the part that gets skipped because admitting a gap feels like handing a reviewer ammunition. It's the opposite: an unnamed gap is a gap nobody's watching, while a named one with its risk stated is a gap someone made a deliberate call about.

nodes.label: Org Shift (roadmap column)
nodes.rationale: Required column, not an afterthought: a roadmap that spends none of its 90 days on who owns the new object and who reports on it produces a pilot that quietly reverts to Stage 1 the moment its original champion moves teams.

nodes.label: Experiment Design Checklist (pre-launch gate)
nodes.rationale: The hypothesis must name a number, not just a direction — only a hypothesis that can fail is actually being tested. Decision Enabled must be stated before launch — a test with no pre-committed decision produces a debate about what the number means instead of an action, which is the outcome the checklist exists to rule out.

nodes.rationale: 'What would falsify this claim' sits before 'what it would take to prove it' and before the confidence rating, deliberately, so it gets written while the claim is still being formed rather than bolted on as a caveat after the recommendation is already drafted and psychologically final.

nodes.label: ICP Scoring Rubric
nodes.rationale: Nine sub-criteria at 0-5 each is deliberately short of exhaustive — a rubric long enough to capture every nuance takes longer to fill out than the qualification call itself, which means it stops getting filled out honestly and reviewers start reverse-engineering the score they already believe. Nine fields fit on one screen during a live call.

nodes.label: Source-of-Truth Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Explicitly marks a prior AI draft (or an AI-generated brand-voice file) as not authoritative, closing the failure where a hallucinated claim gets copied from one AI-generated file into the next, each copy looking more credible for having survived a previous pass.

nodes.label: Brand DNA Spec (toolkit template)
nodes.rationale: Structured fields cost real nuance ('feels fresh and vibrant' captures something a hex code never will), but a narrower spec an agent can check itself against beats a richer one only a person can interpret, because only one scales past a human review queue.

nodes.label: Messaging Pillar Spec
nodes.rationale: Almost every messaging-pillar template stops at support points and proof, leaving the actual failure mode uncovered: a true support point gets stretched by an AI system into an unapproved claim because nothing told it where the line was. The 'do not say' line closes that gap per pillar; capping at three or four pillars keeps the list something a human reviewer and an automated check can both hold in full.

nodes.label: Ridgeline three messaging pillars worked example (Speed to close, Audit-ready by default, Rules finance controls)

nodes.label: Positioning Statement Template (seven slots)
nodes.rationale: A looser positioning brief invites a paragraph of adjectives because nothing forces a specific claim out of the writer. Seven named slots remove that latitude — each demands a fact, not a feeling, and a statement with a blank slot is visibly unfinished rather than vaguely unconvincing, which is what makes it something an AI system can load as a constraint rather than a mood board.

nodes.label: Data Readiness Audit
nodes.rationale: Shared Memory names the schema and assumes the five object types exist; this audit is the question it skips -- whether the org's actual data can populate them.

nodes.label: The Output Chain (structured-handoff test)
nodes.rationale: Test: can the downstream workflow consume this output without a human translating it first? A prose positioning statement fails; the same positioning as a weighted, scoreable ICP model passes.

nodes.label: Understand / Build / Run (three phases)
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing: Understanding must precede Building (nothing to encode Brand DNA for without a defined customer), and Building must precede Running (nothing for Orchestrate to sequence until Design and Attract exist).

nodes.label: Kill-Switch Design (Triggers/Halt Scope/Authority/Recovery)
nodes.rationale: A kill switch designed after an incident is a postmortem action item; designed in advance, it is four decisions made calmly before anyone needs them under pressure.

nodes.label: Envelope, Not Gate (design principle)
nodes.rationale: A gate is passed once at the end; an envelope is a property held continuously while a workflow runs, which is why Govern is drawn as a band beneath all seven workflows, not an eighth box.

nodes.label: Learn -> Sense Feedback Arc
nodes.rationale: The single mechanical difference between a system that compounds and one that resets: without the return arc, every quarter restarts from the same blank assumptions.

nodes.rationale: Reading behavioral data alone (engagement climbing) can produce a confident false positive; adding qualitative and intent signal can reverse the conclusion entirely rather than just adding detail.
